newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM says has no new word on Repap.
newsitem.headline: UPM says has no new word on Repap.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy on Monday declined to comment on a report it would buy Canadian paper group Repap, but said the report was not based on information from CEO Juha Niemela.
Daily Helsingin Sanomat on Sunday carried comments from Niemela, and reported that a decision to buy the Canadian group would come "in the next few weeks".

"During the interview, Niemela said nothing about any plans or about any timetable ... Niemela did not say that we were about to buy Repap," UPM chief spokesman Markku Franssila said by telephone. "We have no comment at all."

Speculation that UPM may buy Repap has revived after a $1.9 million bid by Canada's Avenor failed. UPM has earlier bid for parts of the troubled group and has a stated strategy to become a global paper producer.

According to earlier media reports, Repap's past strategy to buy undervalued paper and pulp mills and modernise them with debt financing have given it modern machinery and a leading position in light-weight-coated paper in North America.
UPM is the world's largest coated magazine paper maker.
